_comment: Hand-labelled ground truth. `live` is the answer a careful reviewer gives with the whole corpus in front of them, and `why` is the evidence — a label without one is an opinion. Edit only with a reason recorded here.
notes: Polymorphic override. `Square.area` is reached only through a call on a base-typed parameter (`shape: Shape` then `shape.area()` in report.py), so nothing names it directly: it is live by dispatch, which the heritage exemption reads off the `Square -> Shape` Extends edge. `Circle.area` shares the name on an unrelated type and must stay dead, which is what keeps the name join from exempting the world. Strict: a live symbol claimed at any tier fails. Confirmed 2026-10-07 by breaking each mechanism and watching `the_extracted_tier_has_no_false_positives` fail: (1) disabling the heritage-override return in `liveness.rs` (the arm that yields `heritage_override_reason`) reported `Square.area` dead at extracted (0.90); (2) disabling `python_parameter_bound_from_type` left `shape.area()` untyped and reported both `Shape.area` and `Square.area` dead at inferred (0.40).

symbols.why: Imported by report.py and the annotation of summarise's parameter; Square's base.
The object passed to summarise is a Square, so `shape.area()` dispatches here; no call names it directly.
Nothing calls it, and Shape declares no `perimeter` to dispatch through.
Same name as Shape.area on a type that does not extend Shape, and no Circle ever exists.
